convention: One lexeme is one dictionary word together with its inflections, suppletive paradigm members and spelling or length variants. A Strong number alone doesn't prove a separate lexeme. A noun and verb sharing letters count separately when Strong gives them separate entries and they have their own meaning and paradigm. Related forms and senses never add to the count. This is the author's count, not an independent certification.

units.why: Strong calls H2063 the irregular feminine of H2088, and OSHB tags the three Pdxms, Pdxfs and Pdxcp. אֵלֶּה serves as their plural.
Strong derives H589 as contracted from H595, and both mean I. Counted conservatively as one pronoun.

keptSeparate.why: Homographs with different functions: object marker and preposition. Strong and OSHB keep them apart.
Verb speak and noun word, with separate entries and paradigms.
Adjective great and verb grow up.
Verb swear, which Strong calls denominative, and the numeral seven.
Light as such and a body that gives light. Strong derives both from one verb.
Head and beginning. Strong derives one from the other, but the meanings and forms differ.
Human being and ground, in separate entries.

notCounted.why: Strong calls it a form of H3824, so it is a related form on the one heart card.
A combining form related to H6235, not a card.
The name Adam isn't a card, and it adds nothing to H0120's count.
